items.reviewedFinding: The masculine follower noun names an adherent of Descartes’s philosophical system; compare the attributive adjective rather than equate noun and adjective ownership.
Historical mite is a tiny, almost imperceptible insect found in cheese; the philosopher comparison reuses the earlier VI minuscule-creature meaning without imposing modern moth taxonomy.

Laisser aller is recorded for not supporting the body or posture; source l’un sur l’autre under laughter is interpreted contextually as bodily leaning, not ordinary movement or a laughter-only meaning.
An adjective relating to metaphysics is listed separately from the feminine discipline noun; source idées métaphysiques requires adjective ownership.

The technical physical adjective having weight/subject to gravity is distinct from heavy and figuratively burdensome. Source enumeration concerns the first property; light objects are not valid distractors.

Autant vaut/vaudrait followed by an infinitive is a preference locution. The source rejoinder is interpreted as might as well not exist, with one canonical meaning across present/conditional surfaces.

items.source: Pierre Larousse, Grand dictionnaire universel du XIXe siècle, volume10, page995, primary dictionary transcription
items.reviewedFinding: The adjective belonging to Malebranche’s system is explicitly separate from the masculine follower noun. Source le philosophe malebranchiste modifies a noun and receives proper adjective ownership.
